items.title: Edmond Hall Interview, 1958-07-18
items.q: The interviewer states 'I know Barnes' and describes buying a car from him. The interviewee (Edmond Hall) does not mention knowing Miller Barnes personally, only responding to the interviewer's story.

ctx.x: Yeah. There's a lot of times that if you do that too much, it gets so you can't help it. Oh, I get to help it. Because that rough tone only good on certain things. Oh, sure. You wouldn't play a nice sweet tune and try to use that but on a blues or something like that. And sometimes you get, you're playing something and you're so anxious that you'll do it all benoins to yourself. Yeah. And if you just keep doing it, you get so you can't help it. Sure. It gets to be a habit. Yeah, it gets to be a habit. This is a…

That I got from Miller Barnes. I know Barnes. He, it's not his regular one but he had this one, saw that it was fair and he said he didn't think he was going to play anymore and did I know anybody who wanted to buy it so I said well I'd like to buy it. That's what started the whole thing. Can you play anything in that one? No, just a few little exercises or so. I can play a little bit of tunes when they're written but I can't… Can't fake anything? No.

Well he's made up a couple of little tunes. Like one day he said he was practicing and came across the first two or three notes of the world is waiting for the sunrise and he's able to go ahead and play the rest of it. So he'll make it all right I think if he can get his fingers to work.
